args.root_cause:
Region file world/region/r.0.0.mca had one corrupt chunk entry at chunk (1,0): decompression failed (zlib "incorrect header check"). On load, Paper logged "Failed to load chunk data ... chunk data will be lost". Cause of the on-disk corruption itself was not determined from available logs. The corrupt entry was last written at 05:50:30 and the file was modified at 08:04:06 by the failed read path.</root_cause>
<parameter name="actions">Checked status (TPS 20, healthy) and logs; grep ERROR showed the chunk read failure for chunk (1,0) in world 'world'. Inspected world/region/r.0.0.mca: 360 chunks ok, chunk 1,0 corrupt. Found backup backups/world-2026-10-31/region/r.0.0.mca with chunk 1,0 ok (saved 05:50:04). Declared incident. Stopped server (world saved on stop). After stop, world/region/r.0.0.mca showed chunk 1,0 as 'ok' but saved 08:05:37, i.e. the shutdown save had overwritten the corrupt entry with the server's in-memory copy, which was not the original player data. Restored only chunk (1,0) via copy_chunk from the backup into world/region/r.0.0.mca; other chunks untouched. Re-inspected: 400 chunks, 0 corrupt, chunk 1,0 saved 05:50:04. Started server. Verified via status (TPS 20, MSPT ~0.6, 2 players online) and logs (no ERROR lines after restart, no chunk load failures). Watched roughly 3.5 minutes.</actions>
<parameter name="resolved">true
args.residual_risk: Chunk (1,0) was restored from the 05:50:04 backup, so any changes made in that chunk between 05:50:04 and the corruption at 05:50:30 (and anything after) are not present in the restored chunk. Only r.0.0.mca was inspected; the other region files (r.-1.-1, r.-1.0, r.0.-1) were not inspected in depth but had no load errors in the logs. The root cause of the original corruption is unknown and could recur. The stop/start disconnected both players (they reconnected). The 08:05:37 shutdown save also rewrote region data for all chunks in r.0.0.mca, which is the normal save behavior.
